verses.text: That same day King Xerxes gave Queen Esther everything Haman, the enemy of the Jews, had owned. Mordecai came before the king, because Esther had told the king how he was related to her.
The king took off his signet ring, which he had taken back from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther put Mordecai in charge of everything Haman had owned.
Esther spoke to the king again. She fell at his feet and cried, begging him to stop the evil plan of Haman the Agagite, the plan he had made against the Jews.
The king held out the gold scepter to Esther. So she got up and stood in front of the king.

She said, "If it pleases the king, if he is pleased with me, if he thinks it is right, and if I please him, let an order be written to cancel the letters Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite wrote. He wrote them to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.
How can I bear to see disaster come on my people? How can I bear to see my family destroyed?"
King Xerxes said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "Look, I have given Esther everything Haman owned, and they have hanged him on the pole because he attacked the Jews.
Now you write another order in the king's name about the Jews, whatever seems best to you. Seal it with the king's ring. No order written in the king's name and sealed with his ring can be canceled."

So right away the king's secretaries were called. It was the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. They wrote down everything Mordecai ordered for the Jews. They wrote to the governors, rulers, and officials of the one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia. They wrote to each province in its own writing and to each people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own writing and language.
Mordecai wrote in the name of King Xerxes and sealed the letters with the king's ring. He sent them by messengers riding fast horses bred for the king's service.

In these letters the king allowed the Jews in every city to gather and defend their lives. They could destroy, kill, and wipe out any armed force of any people or province that attacked them, their children, and their women. They could also take the property of their enemies.
This was to happen on one day in all the provinces of King Xerxes, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
A copy of the order was to be made law in every province and announced to all the peoples, so the Jews would be ready on that day to fight back against their enemies.
The messengers rode out quickly on the royal horses, hurried by the king's command. The order was also announced in the fortress city of Susa.
Mordecai left the king's presence wearing royal clothes of blue and white, a large gold crown, and a purple robe of fine linen. The city of Susa shouted for joy.
For the Jews it was a time of light, happiness, joy, and honor.

In every province and every city where the king's order arrived, the Jews were happy and joyful. They held feasts and celebrated. Many people of other nations became Jews, because they were afraid of the Jews.
